newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico lira issue seen part of government strategy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico lira issue seen part of government strategy.

text.p: Mexico's planned 500 billion Italian lira issue, said to be a five-year floating-rate note, will form part of the country's strategy to create new benchmarks in European currencies, debt analysts said.

On Monday, a Finance Ministry official told Mexican news agency Notimex that the issue, worth about $300 million, will be placed at the end of this week. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is tipped to be lead manager.

Government officials and analysts have said that the United Mexican States, the federal government, is aiming to broaden the base of currencies that it borrows in and could tap other European markets again for relatively small amounts.
Since returning to international credit markets in mid-1995 after the peso crash, the federal government has borrowed in U.S. dollars, deutschemarks and yen.

"It is very much in line with them wanting to create benchmarks in markets at a point in time where they have been really limited to the three major currencies," said Merrill Lynch emerging market debt strategist Joyce Chang.
"If you look at countries like Argentina they have been able to borrow at a lower cost of funding from the European currency markets than from the U.S. dollar market," Chang added.
The issue will be the first lira note launched by the Mexican federal government, and follows a 500 billion lira seven-year issue from Argentina in mid-October.
Argentina also issued two other lira-denominated bonds earlier this year.

"I think it is consistent with their (Mexico's) strategy to diversify from dollar funding. If you look at Argentina, it is doing a similar thing," said Bears Stearns sovereign debt analyst Tulio P. Vera.
By placing a floating rate note, Mexico has less exposure to interest rate fluctuations, analysts said.
The issue is expected to be placed mainly with institutional investors.
Several recent issues by Mexican borrowers have been heavily oversubscribed, and their size bumped up.
The trend by emerging market borrowers such as Mexico away from dollar-denominated borrowing and into the deutschemark and yen markets appears to be widening.

In March this year, Mexican state-owned oil-company Pemex placed a two-year lira fixed rate issue worth about 300 billion lira, or about $192.6 million. The paper had a coupon of 12.25 percent. Pemex swapped the lira into dollars.
Brazil's state-run telecomunnications company Telebras also placed a three-year lira euronote in January this year.
